units.title: Expected work of the actual proximal-query program
units.boundary: The Jensen step in D.4 only, conditional on a finite input gradient second moment. This does not prove the Picard input moment bound (D.7), approximate-query stability, the phase count, total cost (D.8), or either complete paper. Publication admission is tracked separately from compilation.

sources.label: Chen–Chewi–Lu–Zhang, SPHMC Lemma D.4 proof after (D.7)
sources.scope: Attributed expansion of the expectation/Jensen step, not the full lemma.

assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra. V:E→R is C², kappa≥1, and kappa⁻¹‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤‖v‖² for every x,v. The ContDiff assumption makes fderiv a genuine derivative.
Fix 0<eta≤c<1 and eps>0. No eta≤1/2 restriction is introduced. The explicit constant depends only on c.

nu is a probability measure on E and y↦‖gradient V y‖² is integrable. This moment hypothesis must later be established for the actual Picard center law; it is not silently assumed to follow from proximity in total variation.
units.statement: There exist measurable proximal points p and stopping indices N with measurable returned iterate x_N(y), where x_0(y)=y and x_(n+1)(y)=y−eta∇V(x_n(y)). They satisfy p(y)+eta∇V(p(y))=y and ‖x_N(y)−p(y)‖≤eps. The actual finite-fuel interpreter with N(y)+1 fuel returns (x_N(y),N(y)+1). Its real-valued query count is integrable under nu and has the following expectation bound.

steps.title: Use the real stopped program, not an assumed cost certificate
steps.text: The existing execution theorem constructs p and N by contraction and the first successful residual test. Reuse these same witnesses, together with their measurable output, accuracy, and exact interpreter equation. In particular N+1 includes the final successful gradient evaluation.
steps.lean: approximate_proximal_execution supplies hall. Its pointwise work conjunct becomes hbound; its actual execution conjunct is retained in the public conclusion.

steps.title: Establish integrability before taking expectations
steps.text: C² regularity makes the gradient continuous and hence g measurable. The assumed integrable square gives g in L²; on a probability space this implies L¹. The nonnegative logarithm is bounded by g/eps, so it is integrable. The count is measurable, nonnegative, and dominated by an integrable multiple of one plus that logarithm.
steps.lean: memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq and MemLp.integrable supply L¹. Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos and Integrable.mono' prove log integrability; a second domination proves hcount.

steps.title: Apply Jensen on a closed positive domain
steps.text: The variable 1+g/eps lies in [1,infinity). Restrict concavity and continuity of log to this closed convex half-line. Both the variable and its logarithm are integrable, so Mathlib's integral Jensen theorem applies without any improper-log convention.
steps.lean: strictConcaveOn_log_Ioi is restricted to Set.Ici 1; ConcaveOn.le_map_integral checks the domain, closedness and both integrability obligations.

steps.title: Compare the first and second moments
steps.text: Nonnegative variance yields (E g)²≤E(g²). Since g and the square root are nonnegative, E g≤sqrt(E(g²)). This is the Cauchy–Schwarz step on a probability space, using Mathlib's variance identity rather than reproving a generic inequality.

steps.title: Integrate the pointwise work estimate
steps.text: For 0<c<1, both −log c and 1−c are positive, and log((1−c)⁻¹) is nonnegative, so C_c≥0. Integrate the actual count bound, use linearity for the integrable terms, then combine Jensen and log monotonicity. No distributional identification or exchange of limiting integrals is needed.

units.lean_statement: The exact adjacent declaration quantifies the input probability measure, genuine curvature bounds, moment hypothesis, constructed interpreter witnesses and integrable expected cost.
units.lean_proof: The public proof applies the existing actual-execution theorem. A private helper packages Mathlib Jensen, L²-to-L¹ and variance arguments; it has no separate leaf credit. No assumed accuracy or expected-cost oracle replaces the real program.
